config.title: Performance & profiling

intro.title: Performance & profiling
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Python script that measures the execution time of different functions to understand performance basics. You will learn the core concept of profiling, which helps identify slow parts of your code. The main technologies involved are Python's built-in time module and basic function definitions. By the end, you'll be able to write code that profiles performance and makes informed optimizations.
intro.usecase: Performance profiling is essential when building data-intensive applications like real-time analytics dashboards that process millions of records, or e-commerce platforms handling thousands of concurrent user sessions. Developers use profiling tools to identify bottlenecks in database queries, API response times, or data processing pipelines—for example, when a financial dashboard loads slowly due to inefficient aggregation algorithms. This allows teams to optimize critical user flows, such as search filters on large product catalogs or recommendation engines that must return results within milliseconds. Mastering profiling techniques helps ensure applications remain responsive and scalable as they grow in complexity and user base.

objectives: Implement time measurement for code execution using Python's time module
Apply profiling techniques to identify performance bottlenecks in functions
Construct memory usage analysis with the sys module
Configure cProfile to generate detailed performance reports
Manipulate algorithm efficiency by comparing different implementation approaches
Initialize performance benchmarks for critical code sections
Integrate timing decorators to measure function execution across an application

steps.title: Create a timing wrapper function
steps.instruction: Define a function called 'time_function' that takes a function and its arguments, measures execution time using time.time(), and returns the result and duration.
steps.hint: You can use time.time() to get the current time before and after calling the function. Subtract to get the duration.
steps.analogousExample:
# Example of a timing wrapper function
def time_function(func, *args):
    start = time.time()
    result = func(*args)
    end = time.time()
    duration = end - start
    return result, duration
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that can measure the execution time of any given function.
successCriteria: The time_function is defined, uses time.time() to measure duration, and returns both the result and the duration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function uses time.time() and returns both the result and duration.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. The function should take a function and its arguments, measure execution time, and return the result and duration.
